detaileddescription.para: tcp4tlm_bridge is a SystemC/TLM component that tunnels loosely timed TLM transactions over a TCP-based tcp4tlm connection. It is implemented in tcp4tlm_bridge.h and tcp4tlm_bridge.cpp.
The bridge acts in two directions at once:

listitem.para: As a local TLM target through tsckt, it receives local TLM transactions and serializes them into tcp4tlm FlatBuffer messages for a remote peer.
As a local TLM initiator through isckt, it receives remote tcp4tlm messages, reconstructs TLM generic payloads, and forwards them into the local SystemC model.

detaileddescription.para: Two bridge instances can therefore connect two SystemC simulations or component hierarchies across a TCP connection.

sect1.title: Main Interfaces
sect1.para: The tcp4tlm_bridge class derives from:
It exposes the following main interfaces:

listitem.para: tsckt: a TLM target socket for incoming local transactions.
isckt: a TLM initiator socket for executing remote transactions locally.
signals: a vector of sc_out<bool> ports for remote signal updates.
TCP server functionality for receiving peer requests.
TCP client functionality for sending requests to the peer.

sect1.para: The most important configuration parameters are:

sect1.title: Connection Setup
sect1.para: During end_of_elaboration(), the bridge copies other_host_name and other_host_port into the TCP client base class.
During start_of_simulation(), connection setup depends on is_connection_server:

listitem.para: If is_connection_server is true, the bridge starts a local server on this_host_port and waits for the peer to announce its endpoint.

If is_connection_server is false, the bridge connects to the configured remote endpoint, starts its own server, sends a NotifyEndpointMsg containing its local listening endpoint, and waits for an OK response.

sect1.para: When a bridge receives NotifyEndpointMsg, it stores the peer host and port, creates the reverse client connection, sends an OK response, and marks the connection as established.
This handshake creates a bidirectional link: each bridge has a server side for receiving requests and a client side for sending requests.

sect1.title: Forwarding Local TLM Transactions
sect1.para: Local TLM transactions enter the bridge through:
Both callbacks delegate to do_access().
For a read transaction, do_access():

listitem.para: Creates a BusOpMsg containing the current SystemC timestamp, delay, address, data length, access type, and byte enables.
Sends the message through the client connection.
Waits for a BusDataMsg response.
Verifies that the response status is OK and that the response belongs to the original request.
Copies the returned data into the original TLM payload.
Sets the TLM response status to TLM_OK_RESPONSE.

sect1.para: For a write transaction, do_access():

listitem.para: Copies the payload data into a BusOpMsg.
Sends the message through the client connection.
If write_no_response is enabled, marks the transaction as successful after sending.
Otherwise waits for a response and sets the TLM response status according to the received status.

sect1.para: Debug transport is represented as a BusOpMsg with debug access type.

sect1.title: Handling Remote Messages
sect1.para: Incoming tcp4tlm request messages are handled by server_receive_completed().
The bridge supports these request payloads:

listitem.para: NotifyEndpointMsg: announces the peer endpoint and completes the connection handshake.
BusOpMsg: describes a remote TLM bus operation to execute locally.
SyncMsg: carries a peer SystemC timestamp for synchronization.
SigOpMsg: updates one of the bridge's boolean output signals.
NotifyShutdownMsg: requests connection shutdown.

sect1.para: Unhandled messages are logged and answered with a declined response.

sect1.title: Replaying Remote Bus Operations Locally
sect1.para: When server_receive_completed() receives a BusOpMsg, it:

listitem.para: Converts the message into a tlm_generic_payload using init_gp().
Builds a SystemC time point from the message timestamp.
Places a callback task into the asynchronous task queue.
Schedules the task for immediate execution or for the requested simulation time.
Executes the transaction through isckt->b_transport(*gp, delay).
Sends a response back to the peer.

sect1.para: Read requests return BusDataMsg with the data read from the local target. Write requests return an OK or failure response unless the message requested no response.

sect1.title: Time Synchronization
sect1.para: The bridge starts three SystemC threads in its constructor:
timing_thread() coordinates simulation time between peers:

listitem.para: On the non-server side, it periodically sends SyncMsg messages containing the current SystemC timestamp.
On the server side in simulated-time mode, it consumes remote timestamps from next_time_stamp and advances local SystemC time toward them.
On the server side in wall-time mode, it paces simulation against elapsed wall clock time.

sect1.para: process_task_que() moves received network tasks into SystemC execution context. If no_systemc_sync is enabled, or if the requested time point has already passed, tasks run immediately. Otherwise they are scheduled through the payload event queue.
process_timed_task_que() executes tasks when their scheduled SystemC event fires.

sect1.title: Signal Messages
sect1.para: SigOpMsg updates entries in the signals vector. If the message index is valid, the bridge schedules a SystemC task that writes the requested boolean value and then sends an OK response. If the index is out of range, it sends a declined response.

sect1.title: Shutdown
sect1.para: end_connection() sends a final SyncMsg followed by NotifyShutdownMsg when a remote connection is active.
When NotifyShutdownMsg is received, the bridge:

listitem.para: Closes the client socket.
Marks the client connection as disconnected.
Requests server shutdown if the server is still running.
Notifies shutdown_evt inside SystemC context.

sect1.para: The destructor and end_of_simulation() both ensure that the server is shut down and that an orderly shutdown message is sent when appropriate.

sect1.title: Summary
sect1.para: tcp4tlm_bridge is a bidirectional TLM-over-TCP adapter. Local TLM operations are serialized into tcp4tlm messages and sent to a peer, while remote messages are converted back into local TLM transactions and executed through the bridge's initiator socket. The implementation also manages endpoint negotiation, response matching, optional write acknowledgments, simulation-time synchronization, signal propagation, and orderly shutdown.
